title: Lacy mandala — eight rounds
subtitle: Open double-treble fans from round 3 — a 32 cm wall piece or table centrepiece that is more air than yarn
excerpt: The lacy mandala replaces the solid double-crochet base rounds with chain-and-double-treble fans that open up the fabric from round 3 onward. By round 8 the mandala is more air than yarn — a fine-gauge wall piece or table centrepiece that photographs better than a solid version at the same diameter.
sourceNotes: Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886), circular lace motif chapter. Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volumes 1-3 (1885-1890) — the lace doily and fan-round construction.
heroPrompt: A lacy crochet mandala in cream DK cotton on a pale linen background, photographed flat from above in soft daylight — the 32 cm flat circle shows an open lace structure with double-treble fan groups radiating from a solid two-round centre, airy enough to see the surface beneath.

glossaryTerms.definition: UK double treble (dtr): yarn over twice, insert hook, pull up loop, [yarn over, pull through 2 loops] 3 times. Taller than a treble. Called triple crochet (trc) in US patterns.

A group of tall stitches (typically double trebles) worked into the same chain space with chain arches on either side, spreading outward to create an open petal or fan shape. The key texture in the lacy mandala from round 3 onward.
A small decorative loop formed by chaining 3 (or more), then working a slip stitch back into the first chain. Picots sit on the outer edge of lace motifs and edgings as a finishing detail.

content.text: The lacy mandala departs from the solid double-crochet base of the standard mandalas at round 3, switching to
fan
groups of
double-treble

stitches separated by chain-3 arches. Each round the fans expand by one or two double trebles, so by round 7 each of the six fan groups carries five double trebles flanked by chain-3 arches. Round 8 adds a
picot
at each outer point. The finished diameter is 32 cm — slightly larger than the solid eight-round version because the open fans spread the fabric outward.

Blocking is not optional here. The open lace arches between fans contract as they dry, pulling the circle in and distorting the fan shape. Pin all six outer fan tips while the piece is still damp, then pin every chain-3 arch midpoint, apply steam, and leave overnight.

attrs.title: Materials for one motif
attrs.body: About 35 g of DK-weight cotton in one to three colours. A 4 mm crochet hook (UK 8, US G/6). Tapestry needle. Scissors. A large blocking mat and at least 18 blocking pins.

content.text: Gauge

Each finished eight-round lacy mandala measures 32 cm diameter in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook, after steam-blocking. The pre-block measurement will be 2 to 4 cm smaller — always measure after thorough blocking.
Stitches used
chain (ch) — UK and US shared.
slip stitch (sl st) — UK and US shared.
double crochet (dc) — UK; called single crochet (sc) in US patterns. Used in rounds 1 and 2 only.
treble (tr) — UK; called double crochet (dc) in US patterns. Used as anchor stitches beside fan groups.
double treble (dtr) — UK; yarn over twice before inserting hook. Called triple crochet (trc) in US patterns. The main stitch in the fan rounds.
picot — ch 3, sl st into first ch. Outer edging loop on round 8.
magic ring (MR) — adjustable starting loop; no centre hole.
Pattern
Worked in the round, right side facing throughout. Place a stitch marker in the first stitch of rounds 1 and 2. From round 3 onward the fan groups are their own landmarks.
Round 1
Form a magic ring. Ch 1. Work 6 dc into the ring. Sl st to first dc to join. Pull tail to close ring. (6 dc.)
Round 2
Ch 1. Work 2 dc into each stitch around. Sl st to first dc to join. (12 dc.)
Round 3 — First fan round

Ch 4 (counts as first dtr). *Ch 3, 3 dtr into next st, ch 3, dtr into next st. Ch 2*; repeat from * to * four more times. Ch 3, 3 dtr into next st, ch 3. Sl st to top of beg ch-4 to join. (6 fan groups of 3 dtr each, 6 single dtr anchor points, 12 ch-3 arches, 6 ch-2 spaces.)
Round 4

Sl st into first ch-3 sp. Ch 4. 2 dtr into same sp. *Ch 3, dtr into centre of 3-dtr fan, ch 3, 3 dtr into next ch-3 sp. Ch 2. 3 dtr into next ch-3 sp*; repeat from * to * four more times. Ch 3, dtr into centre fan st, ch 3, 3 dtr into next ch-3 sp. Ch 2. Sl st to top of beg ch-4 to join. (6 single dtr points, 12 fan groups of 3 dtr, 12 ch-3 arches, 6 ch-2 spaces.)
Rounds 5 to 7

Each round continues the fan expansion: sl st to first ch-3 sp of the previous round; work (ch 4, 2 dtr into same sp) to begin each fan; ch 3; dtr into each dtr of the previous-round fan; ch 3; close the fan into the next ch-3 sp; ch 2 between fan pairs. Fans grow by one dtr per side per round, so round 5 has fans of 5 dtr, round 6 of 7 dtr, round 7 of 9 dtr. (Round 7 total: 6 fans of 9 dtr, 6 anchor dtr, 12 ch-3 arches, 6 ch-2 spaces.)
Round 8 — Picot edging

If changing colour, fasten off round 7 yarn and join new colour. *Into next ch-3 arch work (2 tr, ch 3, sl st into first ch of ch-3 — picot formed, 2 tr). Into each dtr of the fan work 1 tr with ch 1 between. Into the ch-2 joining space work 1 tr*; repeat from * to * around all six fan groups. Sl st to first tr to join. Fasten off. (6 picot loops at the arch tips; trebles with chain-1 spaces filling the fan tops.)
Chart
The chart reads outward from the magic ring. Rounds 1 and 2 show solid double crochet; rounds 3 to 7 show the expanding double-treble fan groups with chain-3 arches; round 8 shows the picot edging.

definition.title: Lacy mandala — eight rounds
definition.caption: Eight rounds from the magic ring. Rounds 1 and 2: solid flat-circle double crochet. Rounds 3 to 7: expanding double-treble fan groups separated by chain-3 arches. Round 8: picot edging at six outer points.

content.text: Finishing

Fasten off, leaving a 15 cm tail. Thread through a tapestry needle and weave through 4 stitches on the wrong side, reverse direction through 3 stitches, and trim. Weave in the magic ring tail and any colour-change tails. Block on a large foam mat: pin all six outer picot arches first, pulling each to its full length. Then pin the midpoint of every chain-3 arch between fan groups. Apply steam from 3 to 4 cm above the surface and leave pinned overnight.
Joining

The lacy mandala is designed as a standalone piece. If joining into a panel, connect adjacent mandalas through the ch-2 spaces between fan groups using a flat slip-stitch seam, then fill the gaps with small treble hexagons or chain-loop fill-in rounds. The open structure means the joins are barely visible.
Care

Handwash in cool water with mild soap. Do not tumble-dry or wring. Re-block on a foam mat after each wash — the open lace arches will contract without pinning. Allow to dry fully before removing pins.
What to try next

The solid eight-round mandala gives the same diameter but with a denser, heavier fabric better suited to pot holders and bag bases. The lacy hexagon uses the same double-treble fan construction in a six-sided shape — a good next project for applying the fan technique to a different base form.
